claims.text: Ball-milled Mg-Al-Ti-V-Fe-Co powder exhibits a BCC solid solution.
The ball-milled powder is nanocrystalline and has a high defect density.
Milling may leave MgO and TiO2 surface layers on the powder.
SPS at 950–980 °C optimizes precipitation of secondary barrier phases in Mg-Al-Ti-V-Fe-Co.
At 950–980 °C, atomic mobility is sufficient to overcome the nucleation barrier for secondary phases.
The 950–980 °C window activates precipitation without triggering significant magnesium volatility.
Nanometer-scale Mg2Ti- or Al2Ti-type Laves precipitates form at grain boundaries and within the BCC matrix.
TiO precipitates form at grain boundaries and within the BCC matrix.
The Laves and TiO precipitates impede diffusion of metal cations and oxygen anions.
The precipitates promote a dense, continuous passive film rich in TiO2 and Cr2O3-like species.
Precipitation hardening and grain-boundary pinning increase the alloy's hardness.
Barrier-phase precipitation and grain-boundary pinning increase bulk density.
The optimally sintered alloy will exceed 98% theoretical density.
The optimally sintered alloy will have Vickers hardness above 650 HV.
The optimally sintered alloy will have corrosion current density below 0.5 µA/cm² in 0.5 M H2SO4 or 3.5 wt% NaCl.
The optimally sintered alloy will form a 10–20 nm passive film containing a high fraction of TiO2 and Laves-phase-derived oxides.
At or below approximately 800 °C, insufficient diffusion prevents densification and barrier-phase formation.
At 1000 °C or above, magnesium loss, phase decomposition, composition deviation, and porosity degrade corrosion resistance.
Vacuum or high-purity argon minimizes oxygen intake during SPS.
A heating rate of 50–100 °C/min avoids premature magnesium evaporation.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and boundary place magnesium-volatility failure above 1000 °C, whereas the baseline states that a sample sintered at exactly 1000 °C already suffers magnesium loss, porosity, and phase decomposition.
The hypothesis states that insufficient driving force occurs below 800 °C, but the baseline assigns insufficient diffusion, low density, and absent barrier phases to exactly 800 °C.

The stated alloy contains Mg, Al, Ti, V, Fe, and Co but no Cr, while the proposed passive film contains Cr2O3-like species and the experiment calls for a Ti/Cr/Mg ratio without identifying any chromium source.
